newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money softened to 9.0/10.0 percent on Thursday from a high of 11.5 percent on the back of sufficient liquidity, dalers said.

They said adequate supply resulted from a 250 billion injection by the central bank. One local bank dealer said there were concerns over Friday liquidity because of the mid-month factor and weekly tax payments. However, overall rates were stable.
She said there was demand for one-week money to bridge Friday and next Tuesday, which were both anticipated to be slightly tight, but supply was sufficient.
One week-money was at 11.5/12.0 percent. One- and three-month money were at 12.5/12.75 and 13.25/13.50 percent, respectively.
The central bank lowered its three-month bilateral papers (SBIs) by 50 basis points while keeping others unchanged.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 11.24 percent, compared with 14.73 percent on Tuesday.
Bond dealers said activity was dull because focus remained on a slew of new issues soon coming to the market.
